subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) training question for an instant, explained answer — finish your training without second-guessing a marking rule.
metaTitle: CUI Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Marking, handling, and safeguarding CUI.
whyItWorks: CUI training is full of specific marking and handling rules that are easy to blur together — banner markings, category markings, dissemination controls. Cambo reads the exact question and gives you the precise rule that applies, not just the general concept.

options: Information classified at the Confidential level or above
Any information marked For Official Use Only before 2010
Unclassified information that requires safeguarding or dissemination controls under law, regulation, or government-wide policy
Information that has been declassified and released to the public
sampleQuestions.a: Unclassified information that requires safeguarding or dissemination controls under law, regulation, or government-wide policy — it's not classified, but it's not freely releasable either.

sampleQuestions.q: Where should CUI be stored when not in use?
options: In any unlocked desk drawer inside a government building
In a locked container, locked office, or other area with sufficient physical access controls
On a personal device, provided it is password protected
Anywhere, as long as it is shredded at the end of the day
sampleQuestions.a: In a locked container, locked office, or other area with sufficient physical access controls to prevent access by unauthorized individuals.

sampleQuestions.q: What is a "banner marking," in the context of CUI?
options: A watermark applied only to printed copies
A label affixed to the storage container holding the document
A digital signature verifying the author's identity
A header at the top (and often bottom) identifying the document as CUI and specifying its category
sampleQuestions.a: A header placed at the top (and often bottom) of a CUI document that identifies it as CUI and specifies its category — the primary visual indicator that special handling rules apply.

sampleQuestions.q: Can CUI be sent over regular, unencrypted email?
options: No — CUI must be transmitted using approved, encrypted methods
Yes — as long as the recipient is a federal employee
Yes — as long as the subject line includes the CUI marking
Yes — provided the document is attached rather than pasted into the body
sampleQuestions.a: No — CUI must be transmitted using approved, encrypted methods. Sending it over unencrypted email is a common training scenario used to test whether the rule has actually sunk in.

sampleQuestions.q: What is a "dissemination control" marking on a CUI document?
options: A marking indicating how long the information must be retained
A marking that limits who the information may be shared with, separate from the category marking
A marking showing which office originally created the document
A marking indicating the document's classification level
sampleQuestions.a: A marking that limits who the information can be shared with — for example, restricting distribution to federal employees only — separate from the category marking that says what kind of CUI it is.

sampleQuestions.q: Who determines whether a specific piece of information qualifies as CUI?
options: The individual who created the document decides
Any supervisor may designate information as CUI at their discretion
It qualifies only if covered by a law, regulation, or government-wide policy listed in the CUI Registry
The recipient decides based on how sensitive the content appears
sampleQuestions.a: It only qualifies if it's covered by a law, regulation, or government-wide policy listed in the CUI Registry — an individual can't decide on their own that something is CUI without that basis.

faqs.q: How often is CUI training required?
faqs.a: Initial training is required for anyone with access to CUI, with biennial (every 2 years) refresher training required after that.

faqs.q: Who has to take CUI training?
faqs.a: All DoD civilian, military, and contractor personnel who handle or have access to Controlled Unclassified Information.

faqs.q: What's the difference between CUI and classified information?
faqs.a: CUI is unclassified but still sensitive enough to require safeguarding and dissemination controls. Classified information has a formal classification level (Confidential, Secret, Top Secret) with much stricter handling requirements.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or the official CUI program?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense.
Specific types of CUI defined in the CUI Registry, such as Controlled Technical Information, Privacy information, or Export Controlled information, each with its own handling rules.

faqs.q: What score do I need to pass?
faqs.a: Most versions of the course require 70% or better on the final exam to receive a completion certificate.
